patch_description: Replace the random point placement with a deterministic two-phase constructor: (1) fix the four unit-square corners as the convex hull (guaranteeing hull area 1 and a valid convex region), and (2) initialize the 9 interior points as a jittered 3x3 grid (fixed seed) and run a greedy coordinate-descent refinement that repeatedly locates the smallest-area triangle among all 286 triples and perturbs one of its points (with a decaying step size) whenever the perturbation increases the minimal triangle area. This is the classic "worst-triangle-driven" local search for Heilbronn-type problems: since the objective is the min over triangle areas, only moves that involve the currently worst triangle can improve it, making the search both effective and cheap (286 triangle evaluations per candidate, vectorized with NumPy). Multiple deterministic restarts with different seeds keep the best configuration, ensuring reproducibility while substantially raising min_area_normalized well above the 0.03094 benchmark.
